query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The application of a silicide coating to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective silicide layer
generation.mechanism: The silicide coating prevents oxidation of the underlying alloy by forming a barrier against oxygen diffusion
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance and reduced degradation at high temperatures
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 600-1000 °C, atmosphere: air, exposure time: several hours, loading: no external loading
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the silicide coating may depend on the specific composition and processing conditions of the coating and the underlying alloy

falsification_experiment.design: Exposure of coated and uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples to high-temperature air, followed by characterization of the microstructure and oxidation behavior
measurements: Microstructural analysis using SEM and EDS
Oxidation kinetics using TGA or weight gain measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated samples show no significant improvement in oxygen resistance compared to the uncoated samples, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Intervention effect. Base system: MoNbTaTiW RHEA substrate. Intervention: Exposure to Si-20Cr-20Fe coating and high-temperature oxidation. Processing: Coating preparation at 1430°C; oxidation at 1000°C and 1300°C. Test conditions: 1000°C and 1300°C, 1 h. Structure change: Silicide layer moved toward the substrate, protecting the RHEA from oxidation; the coating effectively prevented oxidation of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA. Mechanism: The silicide coating could effectively prevent the oxidation of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The results show that the silicide coating could effectively prevent the oxidation of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA."
